ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, general partners, and authorized signatories must undergo enhanced due diligence screening against the following lists: (1) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list; (2) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (3) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (4) Hong Kong Monetary Authority's Sanctions List; (5) UK HM Treasury Consolidated List; and (6) domestic Chinese sanctions lists. PEP screening must include identification of politically exposed persons (PEPs) as defined by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) recommendations, including family members and close associates. For any PEP identified, senior management approval is required, and enhanced ongoing monitoring must be implemented. Screening must be conducted at onboarding, on a continuous basis (at least daily), and upon any material change. All results must be documented and retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Hong Kong Companies Registry – Name Search and Reservation System (e-Registry)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The name may be in English, Chinese, or both. English names must use Roman letters; Chinese names must use traditional Chinese characters. The name must not be identical or too similar to an existing name. For English names, the order of words is flexible but must not be misleading. For Chinese names, the number of characters is typically 3-6. Transliteration is allowed but must be phonetically accurate. The name must not include any term that implies a connection with the government, any regulated activity, or any prohibited business. The name must not be offensive or contrary to public interest.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 38) of Hong Kong SAR, ss. 3, 4, 19 and 23; Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap. 37) of Hong Kong SAR, ss. 4 to 6, where the Foreign-Invested Partnership elects limited liability; Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310) of Hong Kong SAR, s. 5(1) and s. 5A; Employment Ordinance (Cap. 57) of Hong Kong SAR, s. 50 for the employment agency licence.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Inland Revenue Department of Hong Kong SAR, Business Registration Office, and the Companies Registry of Hong Kong SAR, Limited Partnerships Section for limited partnership registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Business Registration Application Form (B.R. 1) together with the Partnership Particulars Declaration, and where applicable, Limited Partnership Registration Form (LP Form 1) under the Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap. 37).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Under Hong Kong Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 38) and Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap. 37), there is no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Foreign-Invested Partnership and no blocked escrow account is required. The partners may agree the amount and timing of capital contributions in the Partnership Deed; limited partners must make their agreed contributions to retain limited liability status.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE FOREIGN-INVESTED PARTNERSHIP

AT a duly convened and quorate meeting of the Management Committee (the 'Committee') of the Foreign-Invested Partnership (the 'Partnership'), held on this [day] day of [month], [year], at the registered office at [address], Hong Kong SAR, notice of the meeting having been duly waived by all persons entitled to vote, the following resolutions were proposed, seconded and unanimously adopted:

WHEREAS the Partnership was formed as a foreign-invested partnership under the Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap. 37) and the Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 38) of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, and is registered for business under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310);

WHEREAS the Partnership will carry on executive search and headhunting services falling within ISIC 7830, and the partners have agreed to subscribe initial capital, open banking accounts, establish a registered office, and appoint statutory representatives in compliance with law;

WHEREAS the Committee has reviewed the Partnership Deed, the proposed capital contribution schedule, and the terms of the draft banking mandate, and considers such documents to be in the best interests of the Partnership.

NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS RESOLVED THAT:

1. CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND CONTRIBUTIONS. The capital commitments set forth in Schedule A of the Partnership Deed are approved. Each partner shall make the specified capital contribution to the partnership operating account upon written call by the General Partner. All client retainer payments, including wire and Wise B2B deposits, shall be cleared and held in a segregated client money account until invoiced, consistent with the Partnership Deed and applicable Hong Kong and cross-border tax routing rules.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The opening of account number [•] at [Bank] is ratified. The Committee authorizes [Name A] and [Name B] to act as authorised signatories under a dual-signature protocol for all withdrawals, wire transfers, online banking, and foreign exchange transactions over the applicable threshold. Either signatory may issue receipts or deposit instructions, but no two payments in one day may aggregate above the agreed limit without dual approval.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE. The registered office of the Partnership is fixed at [address] in Hong Kong SAR. The Committee appoints the registered address as the place where all summonses, notices, writs, and official communications may be served. The Partnership may appoint a registered agent if the registered office is maintained by a third party.

4. STATUTORY OFFICERS AND FILING POWERS. [Name A] is appointed Chairman of the Committee, [Name B] Compliance Officer and Money Laundering Reporting Officer, and [Name C] Employment Agency Licence Officer. Each officer is vested with authority to execute statutory forms, represent the Partnership before the Inland Revenue Department, Labour Department, and Companies Registry, and make declarations under penalties for perjury as required by law.

5. EFFECTIVENESS. This resolution is effective immediately and may be executed in counterparts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-formation name screening and execution of the Foreign-Invested Partnership Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Hong Kong Companies Registry (Integrated Companies Registry Information System) and a duly licensed Hong Kong solicitor or notary public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed English and Chinese partnership names for an internal conflict check against the Companies Registry database using the Integrated Companies Registry Information System (ICRIS). Execute the Foreign-Invested Partnership Deed before a Hong Kong solicitor or notary, including the capital contribution schedule, profit-sharing percentages, management committee powers, indemnity provisions, and dissolution terms. Verify that the general partner and limited partners satisfy non-resident ownership and identity requirements. Fix a physical registered office address in Hong Kong SAR; a post office box is not acceptable.
required_dossiers: Proposed English and Chinese partnership names
Draft Partnership Deed with capital contribution schedule
Identity documents and proof of address of all partners
Non-resident partner declarations
Consent of proposed management committee members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name screening flags similarity or a prohibited word, the partnership has no formal name reservation; adopt a substantially different legal name and re-execute the Partnership Deed only where the name change affects the deed. If a notary requisitions a corrected identity certificate, provide a newly certified copy within 5 working days and re-attest.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business registration with the Inland Revenue Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Business Registration Office, Hong Kong SAR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of the date of starting business, file the completed business registration application with the Business Registration Office of the Inland Revenue Department. State the partnership's English and Chinese names, the nature of business, the principal place of business, and the names and addresses of all partners. Pay the statutory business registration fee and the levy, and retain the stamped Business Registration Certificate. If any partner is a non-resident of Hong Kong and no partner is resident, the FIP must appoint an authorized representative resident in Hong Kong to receive service of process and official correspondence.
required_dossiers: Completed Business Registration Application Form (B.R. 1)
Certified copy of the Partnership Deed
Identity and address proof of all partners
Proof of registered office address
Business Registration fee and levy payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Business Registration Office issues a query or defect notice, file an amended declaration and any missing identity or address proof within 7 days. If the application is suspended for non-payment, pay the penal levy plus the original fee, submit a written explanation, and obtain a fresh Business Registration Certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration as a limited partnership with the Companies Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Limited Partnerships Section, Hong Kong SAR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form LP1 with the Companies Registry's Limited Partnerships Section before commencing business if the FIP is to have limited liability for limited partners. Attach a certified copy of the Limited Partnership Deed, a signed statement of capital contributions, and proof of the general partner's identity. The form must be executed by all partners or their lawful attorneys and accompanied by the prescribed fee. Upon verification, the Companies Registry issues a Limited Partnership Registration Certificate; the FIP must not hold itself out as a company, because it is a partnership.
required_dossiers: Form LP1 signed by all partners or their attorneys
Certified true copy of the Limited Partnership Deed
Statement of agreed capital contributions
Identity documents of the general partner and limited partners
Proof of the Hong Kong registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Registry issues a requisition, respond in writing within 14 days. If the defect relates to the deed, have all partners execute an amending deed, re-certify the copy, and re-file Form LP1 together with the requisition response. If the registration is refused, seek judicial review or a fresh application after curing the capacity defects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for the Employment Agency Licence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Hong Kong Labour Department, Employment Agencies Administration (EAA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application to the Employment Agencies Administration of the Labour Department using the official Form EAA-1 before prosecuting any executive search placement. Attach the Partnership Registration Certificate, the Business Registration Certificate, proof of the registered office, and a criminal record declaration of each applicant and the designated manager. Demonstrate that the manager has the prescribed relevant experience and that the applicant is a fit and proper person to operate an employment agency. Pay the licence fee; the licence must be displayed conspicuously at the office and renewed according to the prescribed validity period.
required_dossiers: Form EAA-1 completed and signed
Limited Partnership Registration Certificate
Business Registration Certificate
Criminal record declaration of each applicant and designated manager
Proof of registered office and any branch office address
Employment Agency Licence fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Labour Department refuses, suspends or attaches conditions to the licence, submit written representations to the Employment Agencies Administration within 14 days. If the refusal is upheld, file an appeal to the Administrative Appeals Board within 21 days under section 51 of the Employment Ordinance (Cap. 57), and cure any fitness-related dilapidations in the manager's declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-formation compliance onboarding, banking activation and office clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial institution (bank), Inland Revenue Department, and Hong Kong Fire Services Department / Buildings Department for office premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the corporate bank account under the banking mandate approved by the Management Committee, and complete customer due diligence, beneficial ownership declarations and risk assessment of target payment rails including retainer wire and Wise B2B. Engage a registered fire service contractor to inspect and certify the office's fire safety installations including extinguishers, emergency lighting, and exit signage. Notify the Inland Revenue Department of payroll tax obligations, and update the Business Registration and Employment Agency Licence particulars for any change in branch address or officer appointment. Because the business is office-based executive search with no manufacturing, no Environmental Impact Assessment, Civil Defense licence, or hazardous waste permit is required.
required_dossiers: Banking mandate approved by the Management Committee
Beneficial ownership declaration forms
Fire Services Installations Certificate or equivalent inspection report
Office tenancy agreement or occupation permit
AML/CFT policy manual
Updated list of officers and their identification documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the financial institution raises a query on beneficial ownership, submit a certified legal opinion, the updated Partnership Deed and a Certificate of Incumbency. If the Fire Services Department or Buildings Department flags a deficiency, complete remedial works with a registered fire service contractor and obtain a fresh certificate of compliance within 14 days, then submit the requalification evidence to the relevant department.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Hong Kong Labour Department, Employment Agencies Administration (EAA)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Department (EPD), Hong Kong SAR
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable / Exempt - pure office-based executive search and headhunting agency; no ISIC 1xxx, 2xxx, 3xxx, 4xxx or 52xx physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing operations; therefore no Environmental Impact Assessment report is required under the EIA Ordinance (Cap. 499).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - zero industrial wastewater, VOC, hazardous waste or point-source emissions; ordinary office sewage and municipal refuse must be disposed of through the public sewerage system and licensed waste collectors under the Waterworks Ordinance (Cap. 102) and the Waste Disposal Ordinance (Cap. 354).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no Civil Defense fire permit is required for a non-industrial office under the Fire Safety Ordinance (Cap. 502); however, the executive search office must comply with general fire safety and occupational health standards, including a Fire Services Installations Certificate, adequate emergency exits, and structural occupancy clearance under the Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) and the Occupational Safety and Health Ordinance (Cap. 509).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, acting through the Commissioner of Inland Revenue; electronic tax portal: eTAX (https://www.etax.gov.hk). The Business Registration Office operates under the IRD pursuant to the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Confirm the Hong Kong partnership is validly formed, including a limited partnership under the Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap. 37) or a general partnership at common law, and, because the activity is executive search/headhunting, obtain an Employment Agency Licence under Part XII of the Employment Ordinance (Cap. 57) from the Labour Department; this licence is a separate non-tax business licence. Step 2: Within one month of commencing business in Hong Kong, apply for Business Registration via eTAX or at the IRD Business Registration Office. The foreign non-resident partnership must use the prescribed application form under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310) and provide: the partnership agreement or deed; certificates of registration or incorporation from the partners' home jurisdictions; valid identity documents of all partners; the Hong Kong principal place of business address; and a description of the business as ISIC 7830 executive search and headhunting. Step 3: The IRD will issue a Business Registration Certificate with a Business Registration Number (BRN); the BRN is the statutory tax identifier for the partnership and is used for all IRD correspondence, including any partnership Profits Tax Return. Step 4: If employees are engaged, register the partnership as an employer with the IRD for Salaries Tax and employer return obligations under the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112); Hong Kong does not impose payroll tax withholding, but employer reporting obligations apply. Step 5: For non-resident partners without a Hong Kong place of business or habitual residence, appoint a Hong Kong tax representative to receive IRD notices and to comply with assessment and information requests.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None comparable to a check-the-box election. A Hong Kong partnership is statutorily fiscally transparent: no profits tax is charged at partnership level; each partner is assessable on their share of Hong Kong-source partnership profits under the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112), subject to the territorial source principle. Hong Kong law does not permit a partnership to elect entity-level taxation. Individual partners resident in Hong Kong may elect Personal Assessment under Part VII of the Inland Revenue Ordinance, but that election does not alter the partnership's pass-through classification. There is no domestic hybrid-mismatch election regime in Hong Kong.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT/GST/Sales and Use Tax (Hong Kong has no general indirect tax; the only indirect duties are those under the Dutiable Commodities Ordinance (Cap. 109), which do not apply to executive-search services).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable - there is no indirect tax registration threshold in Hong Kong. The only statutory registration trigger is the commencement of a business in Hong Kong under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310), irrespective of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. Hong Kong does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, API integration, e-invoicing reporting, or anti-fraud digital stamping. Businesses may use paper or electronic invoices, and must keep records in English or Chinese sufficient to enable assessable profits to be readily ascertained under Section 51C of the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable in Hong Kong because there is no VAT or GST to zero-rate. For profits tax purposes, cross-border executive-search fees may be treated as non-Hong-Kong-source offshore income if the services are performed, negotiated, and delivered wholly outside Hong Kong; eligibility depends on the substantive location of the headhunting work, not merely on the invoicing address or foreign client status.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: No Hong Kong customs export declaration, Bill of Entry, or Bill of Lading is required for cross-border executive-search services, because no physical goods are exported and services are not subject to customs duties under the Dutiable Commodities Ordinance (Cap. 109).

For an offshore-income claim, maintain: (a) the signed executive-search retainer agreement with the foreign client showing the engagement's place of performance; (b) itemised invoices issued by the Hong Kong partnership to the foreign client; (c) bank remittance receipts or SWIFT MT103 credit advices from the foreign client evidencing fee settlement; (d) work-product files, candidate sourcing records, interview notes, and time records evidencing that the headhunting activities physically occurred outside Hong Kong; and (e) email or meeting records demonstrating negotiation and execution of the engagement outside Hong Kong.
Hong Kong has no foreign-exchange controls and the IRD does not require an Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC); a standard bank-in or remittance advice is sufficient evidence of payment.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: There is no VAT zero-rating to claw back because Hong Kong imposes no VAT or GST. If a partnership or partner claims offshore treatment and the IRD determines the services were performed in Hong Kong, the IRD may raise additional profits tax assessments under the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112). For incorrect returns without reasonable excuse, additional tax of up to 100% of the tax undercharged may be imposed under Section 82A of the Inland Revenue Ordinance, and criminal penalties may apply for fraudulent tax evasion. The IRD may also impose business registration penalties under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310). In audit, the IRD typically requests engagement contracts, time records, email communications, bank statements, travel records of personnel, evidence of the foreign client's location, and candidate interview records. No 180-day foreign-currency repatriation deadline applies in Hong Kong.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) as the de facto central bank and currency board authority; the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) and People's Bank of China (PBOC) govern the mainland Chinese renminbi and capital-flow elements of this Foreign-Invested Partnership
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Hong Kong dollar is fully convertible and freely floating within the institutional window of 7.75 to 7.85 Hong Kong dollars per United States dollar under the Linked Exchange Rate System supervised by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority. Hong Kong imposes no exchange controls; current-account and capital-account transactions are unrestricted for residents and non-residents, and foreign currency can be held, remitted, and settled without prior authorization. For the mainland Chinese nexus of this Foreign-Invested Partnership, the renminbi remains under a managed float with controls exercised by the State Administration of Foreign Exchange and the People's Bank of China. Trade-related service fees, including executive-search retainer invoices, may be settled with genuine contracts and bank verification. Capital contributions into the mainland entity require FDI registration, a SAFE foreign-exchange registration certificate, and settlement through a designated domestic bank within the approved capital account limit. Profit distributions to offshore partners are subject to tax clearance and CRS reporting, but Hong Kong imposes no surrender or conversion requirement. The convertibility of CNY proceeds generated by the mainland FIP is conditional on supporting documentation and cannot be used to bypass SAFE capital controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Hong Kong has no statutory surrender timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio. Export proceeds may be retained in any currency without compulsory exchange. For a mainland Chinese affiliated entity, SAFE requires goods-export foreign-currency receipts to be repatriated into a domestic foreign-exchange account within 90 days of the customs declaration date; conversion into CNY is voluntary after verified reporting through the Trade Monitoring System, and the enterprise may keep the foreign exchange in a settlement account up to the verified balance. Service-export proceeds, such as cross-border headhunting fees, follow the same repatriation and verification framework but must be declared under the service-trade foreign-exchange purpose code.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating is medium-high for the Hong Kong treasury node and low for the mainland China Foreign-Invested Partnership. In Hong Kong, licensed stored-value facility operators and money service operators under the HKMA and the Customs and Excise Department may hold operating balances and process cross-border payments; Wise B2B is acceptable only as an ancillary rail from the Hong Kong entity. In mainland China, the FIP cannot legally maintain its primary corporate settlement account with an overseas fintech EMI because SAFE and PBOC require corporate settlement, foreign-exchange verification, and tax declaration to be performed only by domestic designated banks. Therefore, regulatory capital injections, tax payments, and trade-verified disbursements must never be routed through Wise or any unlicensed EMI.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the HKMA anti-money-laundering guideline, non-face-to-face account opening via video KYC is permitted, but tier-1 Hong Kong commercial banks generally require the general partner and at least two authorized signatories to complete an in-branch due-diligence interview on first onboarding. Remote consular proxy opening is rarely accepted as a full substitute; some banks allow a non-face-to-face account only with enhanced customer due diligence, legal certification, and independent verification of the partnership deed. For the FIP, personal appearance of the general partner is effectively mandatory unless the bank has adopted a fully approved institutional digital onboarding process.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Limited partnership structure with non-resident partners and nominee ownership that obscures the ultimate beneficial owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified partnership agreement, statutory declaration of the ultimate beneficial owners, register of partners containing national IDs and passports, consolidated ownership chart signed by the general partner, and source-of-wealth statements with bank statements for every natural person holding ten percent or more of the partnership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and politically-exposed-persons screen mismatch due to dual China/Hong Kong nationality or name transliteration variants.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Passport and permanent residence permits, Hong Kong identity card, signed sanctions and PEP self-declaration, negative media screening output from an independent vendor, Business Registration Certificate, Companies Registry record, and a licensed law-firm legal opinion verifying identity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border service invoice discrepancy between headhunting retainer amounts and actual placement milestones, raising trade-mispricing or money-laundering concern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed executive-search agreement with clear scope and fee milestones, itemized invoice breakdown, candidate-submission and time records, placement confirmation letters from the hiring enterprise, and client bank reference letters.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital contribution from offshore partners into the mainland FIP unsupported by a completed foreign-direct-investment registration.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE foreign-exchange registration certificate, MOFCOM filing receipt, capital-contribution wire with correct SAFE purpose code, CPA-issued capital verification report, and written undertaking from all partners confirming that no third-party intermediary or unlicensed funding source was used.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route the capital contribution from the Hong Kong treasury account to the mainland FIP capital account by SWIFT MT103. The wire must include the SAFE transaction purpose code for foreign-direct-investment capital contribution and the unique FDI registration file number. The mainland designated bank will match the payment against MOFCOM and SAFE records, restrict the capital account to the approved amount, and require a certified Chinese CPA capital verification report before any disbursement. Renminbi converted from the capital account may be used only for the foreign-invested partnership's business scope, including executive-search consultant payroll, supplier fees, and operating leases; it may not be applied to securities investment or entrusted lending outside the negative list.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Executive-search client fees and disbursements should clear through SWIFT MT103 using the operative account in Hong Kong. Commercial letters of credit and documentary collections are inappropriate for pure headhunting services and should be reserved for any ancillary goods purchases. For payments to mainland beneficiaries, use offshore renminbi clearing via the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's Clearing House Automated Transfer System (CHATS) with a CNH settlement message that includes the service-trade invoice reference and the correct SAFE settlement code. Beneficiary names and account numbers must be exact and fully populated to avoid AML intervention.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable HKD/USD forward contracts within the 7.75 to 7.85 currency-board band
Offshore CNH deliverable forwards between the Hong Kong treasury and licensed counterparties
CNH non-deliverable forwards for hedging mainland renminbi exposure without physical settlement
Cross-currency swaps and simple FX options aligned with retainer billing cycles and payroll liabilities

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employment Agency Licence Annual Renewal under the Employment Agency Regulations (Cap. 57A) for Licensed Executive Search and Headhunting Agency
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Application for renewal must be received on or before the expiry of the current licence; submission is normally accepted from 2 months before expiry and is recommended no later than 30 days before expiry. There is no statutory grace period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operating without a valid employment agency licence is a criminal offence under the Employment Ordinance; upon conviction the operator is liable to fine and imprisonment. The EAA may refuse renewal, revoke the licence, and effectively terminate the headhunting business until a fresh licence is obtained.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Registration Certificate Annual Renewal (Business Registration Ordinance, Cap. 310)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department - Business Registration Office (BRO)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payment of the annual statutory fee and levy must be made by the expiry date shown on the Business Registration Certificate or the related IRD Demand Note, ordinarily on or before the 12-month anniversary of the commencement date or the certificate issue date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late payment surcharge of HK$300 is imposed for overdue renewal. Carrying on business without a valid Business Registration Certificate is an offence, and the BRO may deregister the business from the Business Register; continued non-compliance may lead to administrative strike-off of the registration, restoration costs, and loss of ability to enforce contracts in the business name.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Partnership Profits Tax Return (BIR52 Series) for the Foreign-Invested Partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) - Profits Tax Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The return must be filed within 1 month of the date of issue. Where a recognised Hong Kong tax representative is appointed and an extension is requested, a 31 December year-end is generally extended to 15 August of the following year; deadlines for other year-ends follow the IRD Annual Extension Schedule for Tax Representatives.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file allows the IRD to raise an estimated assessment under section 59(3) of the Inland Revenue Ordinance (IRO). Wilful failure without reasonable excuse may lead to prosecution, a fine of up to HK$10,000, and additional tax of up to three times the amount of tax undercharged under section 82A. There is no administrative strike-off for tax non-payment alone, but prolonged default can trigger seizure and bankruptcy/insolvency action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return of Remuneration and Pensions (BIR56A / BIR56B) for Employees of the Headhunting Agency
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) - Employer's Return Processing Section
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month from the issue date, ordinarily on or before 1 May for the year of assessment ending 31 March, unless an electronic filing extension has been expressly granted by the IRD.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing is an offence under section 80(1) of the IRO, subject to a fine of up to HK$10,000 and additional tax of up to three times the amount undercharged where incorrect returns are made; the IRD may also issue estimated assessments and take recovery proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Internal Confirmation of Limited Partnership Particulars and Event-Based Notice of Changes (where the FIP is registered as a Limited Partnership under the Limited Partnerships Ordinance, Cap. 37)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies Registry (for notifiable changes) and internal statutory records (for annual confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: There is no fixed annual return for a Cap. 37 limited partnership; however, any change to the name, nature of business, principal place of business, partners, or capital contributions must be filed with the Companies Registry within 7 days of the change. The partnership should perform and document an annual confirmation of its statutory register on or before each formation anniversary.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to notify the Registrar within 7 days or knowingly submitting a false statement is an offence under Cap. 37 and may result in fines and imprisonment. Continued breach can expose the limited partners to the risk of losing limited liability protection and can lead to administrative rejection of the partnership registration standing.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Part 9 of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), every active Hong Kong incorporated company must appoint a certified public accountant and have its financial statements audited in accordance with Hong Kong Standards on Auditing. There is no general statutory audit exemption based on balance-sheet size, turnover, or headcount for active companies; the only relevant quantitative/dormancy carve-out is that a company is audit-exempt only if it is dormant under section 5 and files the applicable declaration of no accounting transactions. A non-incorporated Foreign-Invested Partnership is not automatically subject to audit under the Partnership Ordinance unless a corporate partner is itself a Hong Kong company, the partnership is structured as a Limited Partnership Fund under Cap. 637 with an audit provision in its fund documentation, the Securities and Futures Commission requires audited accounts, or the IRD calls for certified accounts in connection with an investigation or through a notice.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS), which are materially aligned with IFRS issued by the IASB, are the applicable statutory accounting framework. Eligible private entities without public accountability may apply the HKFRS for Private Entities standard. For non-corporate partnerships without a statutory audit requirement, accounts may be maintained on a tax-basis for Inland Revenue Ordinance compliance, but any voluntarily or contractually audited financial statements must still follow HKFRS or an acceptable agreed-upon framework approved by the appointed CPA.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong does not require an annual UBO confirmation filing for ordinary partnerships. If the Foreign-Invested Partnership is registered as a limited partnership under Cap. 37, any change in limited partners or contribution amounts must be notified to the Companies Registry within 7 days. If any partner is a Hong Kong company, that company must maintain a Significant Controllers Register (SCR) as required by the Companies Ordinance, and the SCR must be updated within 15 days of any change in significant controllers. There is no 30-day UBO shareholding transfer filing requirement for Hong Kong partnerships; share transfers in a corporate partner are recorded in that company's register of members and reflected in the SCR as promptly as its articles require.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (maintained by any corporate partner that is a Hong Kong company)
Register of Directors (maintained by any corporate partner that is a Hong Kong company)
Register of Partners (maintained for a Cap. 37 limited partnership)
Significant Controllers Register (SCR) (maintained at the Hong Kong registered office or by the corporate partner)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 770 - USD 2,560 per annum (approximately HKD 6,000 - HKD 20,000) for Hong Kong registered office, registered agent, and transversal corporate secretarial support.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,030 - USD 3,850 per annum (approximately HKD 8,000 - HKD 30,000) for a small to mid-sized headhunting agency or corporate partner if an audit becomes applicable; a pure partnership tax accounts compilation without statutory audit generally costs USD 640 - USD 1,920 per annum.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Hong Kong territorial source system: only profits arising in or derived from Hong Kong are chargeable; two-tiered Profits Tax rates for unincorporated partnerships (7.5% on first HK$2 million assessable profits, 15% on remainder for individual partners; corporate partners use 8.25% / 16.5%); 300% tax super-deduction for qualifying R&D expenditure (first HK$2 million) and 200% for the excess; no capital gains tax, no VAT/GST, no dividend withholding tax; foreign-sourced income exemption (FSIE) is available only if the FIP meets the 2023 economic substance requirements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: BIR52 - Profits Tax Return (Partnership), filed through the Inland Revenue Department's eTax portal and Integrated Tax System (ITS) by an authorized Hong Kong tax representative
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual - one BIR52 is issued for each year of assessment; basis period is the partnership accounting period ending in the previous year of assessment
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within one month from the date of issue of the BIR52; where the FIP is represented by an authorized Hong Kong tax representative, the IRD normally grants an automatic extension of 3-5 months (e.g., for a fiscal year ended 31 December 2023, the extended e-filing due date is 15 August 2024).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: General partnership particulars: legal name of the Foreign-Invested Partnership, Hong Kong Business Registration Number, principal place of business, commencement/cessation date and accounting period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact legal name and BR number of the FIP. If the general partner or controlling partner is non-resident, use the tax representative's Hong Kong address as the contact place of business. Attach the partnership agreement and clearly disclose the non-resident partner list; failure to attach the register is treated as a defective non-resident declaration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit or loss per audited financial statements before taxation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The audited P&L must be in Hong Kong dollars and must fully record cross-border retainer fees from mainland Chinese clients. Any retainer paid to a nominee or routed through an offshore bank without a corresponding service contract is a red flag and will be reconstructed by the IRD as assessable profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs: non-deductible expenses, private expenses, depreciation, penalties, fines, entertainment above statutory limits and illegal bribes/kickbacks.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back success fees paid to a zero-substance offshore entity that renders no actual executive-search services. A payments commission without CIGA in Hong Kong is non-deductible under the Inland Revenue Ordinance; if a non-resident partner has personally received such fees, the add-back must be grossed up and disclosed in the partner allocation schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exclusion of tax-exempt income, non-assessable offshore profits and FSIE-qualifying foreign-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only profits arising in or derived from Hong Kong are chargeable. For executive headhunting, the source is generally where candidate identification, evaluation, client negotiation and placement contracts are effected. A blanket offshore claim is fatal unless the partnership maintains contemporaneous evidence of overseas CIGA. Non-resident partners must not assume automatic offshore treatment; under the 2023 FSIE rules, substance in Hong Kong must be demonstrated for any excluded passive income and for offshore active income claims.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital allowances and balancing charges: qualifying fixed assets such as computers, CRM software, office equipment and leasehold improvements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only assets physically used in the Hong Kong headhunting business. Assets of an overseas non-resident partner's home office are not allowable. All invoices and customs/importation records must identify the Hong Kong FIP as owner; otherwise the IRD will disallow the deduction and add back the full cost.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss relief set-off and adjusted loss: carry-forward partnership tax losses set off against assessable profits of the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Hong Kong partnership losses may be carried forward indefinitely, but are allocated to partners in accordance with the profit-sharing deed. A non-resident partner may set off its share of Hong Kong losses only against Hong Kong-source assessable profits; it cannot use such losses against mainland Chinese or other foreign-source income. The partnership return must state the loss allocation separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partner allocation schedule: each partner's name, tax file number, residency status, profit-sharing ratio, share of adjusted assessable profit/loss and share of tax payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the operative non-resident tax declaration. Identify each non-resident partner's country of residence, Tax Residency Certificate (if any), Hong Kong tax representative and Hong Kong address for service of assessment. The FIP is pass-through; the IRD assesses each partner directly on his/her agreed share. The partnership may be appointed as agent for collection under the Inland Revenue Ordinance, so the return must truthfully state the non-resident partners' capital and profit shares.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration and signature of the partnership tax representative.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Hong Kong tax representative signs the return and declares that the allocation schedule, source declarations and transfer pricing information are complete and correct. A knowingly false declaration exposes the representative and the controlling partner to personal criminal liability for tax evasion, fraud and misrepresentation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or failure to file BIR52 without reasonable excuse: (i) fine of HK$10,000 under IRO s.80(1); (ii) daily default penalty of HK$50 per day for continuing default; (iii) the IRD may issue an estimated assessment under s.59(3); (iv) if the late return shows undercharged tax, the IRD may impose penalty tax of up to 10% of the undercharged tax (minor case), 50% (ordinary neglect) or 100% (willful fraud); (v) fraudulent evasion of tax under s.82 carries a fine of HK$100,000 plus treble the amount of tax undercharged, and imprisonment for 3 years; the court can also order seizure of personal assets and issue a departure restriction order preventing the director/partner from leaving Hong Kong until the tax debt is settled.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - Hong Kong does not impose any withholding tax on dividends or partnership profit distributions. A distribution from the FIP to a non-resident partner is not subject to WHT, but the non-resident partner remains chargeable to Profits Tax on its allocated share of profits arising in Hong Kong.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Because Hong Kong imposes no dividend WHT, no treaty relief is required for distributions. For Hong Kong-sourced royalties paid to non-resident beneficial owners, the payer must withhold at the statutory profits tax rate unless the comprehensive DTA reduces the rate. To claim DTA relief the taxpayer must: (1) obtain an approved Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the non-resident's tax authority or, for Hong Kong residents, apply for a Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate from the IRD; (2) complete and file the relevant IRD application for treaty relief before payment; (3) provide a beneficial ownership declaration supported by board resolutions, audited financial statements and underlying royalty/licence agreements; (4) prove the non-resident is the true legal and economic owner of the royalty income and is not an agent/nominee; and (5) maintain contemporaneous evidence of the intercompany licence, place of management, and CIGA. Late or unsupported claims are rejected and the full statutory rate is recovered.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate on royalties paid to a non-resident for the use of or right to use intellectual property in Hong Kong: 16.5% for corporate recipients and 15% for individual non-residents, unless reduced by a DTA. Interest paid to non-residents is generally not subject to Hong Kong WHT because the IRD does not ordinarily tax non-resident passive interest unless it is derived from a Hong Kong trade/profession; if chargeable, it is taxed at the standard profits tax rate. Under the Mainland/Hong Kong tax arrangement, the approved DTA rates are generally 5% for royalties and 7% for interest; other Hong Kong DTAs often reduce royalty WHT to 0-10%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: HKD 5 million in aggregate specified transactions triggers Local File preparation; global consolidated group revenue of HKD 680 million or more triggers Master File preparation, in accordance with the Inland Revenue Ordinance and DIPN 58.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The FIP must demonstrate real economic substance in Hong Kong. For the 2023 foreign-sourced income exemption (FSIE) and treaty benefits, the IRD will examine whether the Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) - such as candidate sourcing, reference checking, placement contract negotiation, fee invoicing and management decisions - are actually performed in Hong Kong. The FIP must keep fixed office premises in Hong Kong, have local employees/decision-makers, and maintain complete records proving the economic substance; a shell headhunting FIP with no CIGA is outside the exemption and full Profits Tax will apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion, False Profits Tax Return and FSIE Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing BIR52 showing nil assessable profit by asserting that all executive-search income is foreign-sourced when in fact candidates, clients and placement contracts are managed in Hong Kong; routing client fees through shell bank accounts and issuing fake invoices from a zero-substance offshore recruiting vehicle.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue Ordinance (IRO) s.82(1) - fraudulent evasion of tax: fine of HK$100,000 plus treble the amount of tax undercharged, and imprisonment for 3 years; the IRD may also raise estimated assessments under s.59(3) and penalty assessments of up to 100% of undercharged tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The court may pierce the FIP's limited liability structure and hold the controlling general partner and directors of the corporate general partner personally liable. Civil remedies include restitution of diverted corporate assets, seizure and garnishment of personal assets, travel restriction/blacklisting at Hong Kong immigration, disqualification and criminal imprisonment for up to 3 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure and Artificial Intercompany Margin
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying a 60% success fee to a related Cayman Islands research and sourcing company that has no staff, no office, no records and no actual headhunting functions; failing to prepare Hong Kong TP documentation despite aggregate intercompany specified transactions exceeding HKD 5 million, and incorrectly treating the entire fee stream as non-Hong Kong sourced.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: IRO s.58C and DIPN 58 - failure to prepare/maintain Transfer Pricing documentation: fine of up to HK$50,000 under s.80(2) plus daily default penalties; the IRD may reconstruct the intercompany fee at arm's length and impose penalty tax of 10% to 100% of the undercharged tax; cases involving deliberate evasion carry s.82 fines and imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve inflated related-party fees are personally liable for the resulting tax undercharge; civil judgments may require restitution of the disallowed fees from personal assets; a travel ban and immigration blacklisting can be issued; criminal conviction carries imprisonment for up to 3 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, Shell Company Arrangement and Unlicensed Money Transmission
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The FIP functions as an unlicensed clearing house for executive-search retainers paid by mainland Chinese principals and success-fee kickbacks to another shell entity in a highly rated-AML blacklisted jurisdiction; no KYC/CDD is performed on true beneficial owners, nominee partners conceal the actual controllers, and the partnership has no physical Hong Kong office or bank records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615) s.12 - carrying on an unlicensed money service: fine and imprisonment on summary conviction; Organized and Serious Crimes Ordinance (Cap. 455) - possession/proceeds of crime: restitution, confiscation, and imprisonment up to 14 years; Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310) s.6 - failure to register: fine of HK$5,000 and imprisonment for 1 year.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The court will lift the corporate veil: nominee directors and controlling partners are jointly and severally liable for civil asset restitution, confiscation orders and the unpaid tax; the High Court may impose a travel ban/blacklisting to prevent departure; directors face criminal imprisonment up to 14 years for money laundering and up to 3 years for tax evasion.
